title: Brain Dissection Protocol
author: Ana Catarina Carapinha Cascalho
materials: Ensure all tools and materials are sterilized.
Wear appropriate personal protective equipment like a lab coat and gloves.
Lift the brain out of the skull gently.

steps.title: Prepare workspace
steps.instruction: Set up a clean and organized workspace.

steps.title: Euthanize by cervical dislocation
steps.instruction: Use cervical dislocation (no anesthesia) to minimize anesthesia‑related effects.

steps.title: Remove head
steps.instruction: With surgical scissors, cut posterior from the ears and remove the head.

steps.title: Make midline skin incision
steps.instruction: Make a midline incision in the skin using scissors.

steps.title: Expose skull
steps.instruction: Flip the skin over the eyes to expose the skull.

steps.title: Incise top of skull
steps.instruction: Use Iris scissors to make a small incision on the top of the skull, starting from the caudal part at the interparietal bone, taking care not to cut through brain tissue.

steps.title: Cut anterior skull
steps.instruction: Make a firm cut through the most anterior part of the skull (frontal bone) between the eyes to facilitate easier brain removal.

steps.title: Remove parietal bones
steps.instruction: Tilt one side of the parietal bone with curved narrow‑pattern forceps and break it off; repeat for the other side. If the frontal bone remains, make a small incision to facilitate its removal.

steps.title: Detach brain from meninges
steps.instruction: Carefully avoid damaging the meninges. Once the brain is free from meninges, slide the closed curved narrow‑pattern forceps under the anterior brain (olfactory bulb), gently tilt upward to lift the brain, then slide the forceps further down to break the optic nerves and other cranial nerves.

steps.title: Wash brain
steps.instruction: Wash the brain thoroughly with ice‑cold DPBS (Sigma; D8662) on a gelatin plate.

steps.title: Hemisphere separation
steps.instruction: Cut the brain into left and right hemispheres.

steps.title: Dissect regions of interest
steps.instruction: Depending on experimental needs, dissect the following areas: cerebellum, cortex, interbrain, hindbrain.

steps.title: Transfer to tubes
steps.instruction: Place dissected brain parts in appropriately labeled tubes.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze and store
steps.instruction: Snap‑freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen, handle tissues carefully to avoid damage, work quickly to preserve integrity, and store frozen brain parts at –80 °C until further analysis.
